description: An anonymous 17th-century French etching shows a seated, richly dressed nobleman with a dog, receiving a money bag, a basket of fruit and a sack of grain from a thin, bearded peasant. A spider web with a spider and trapped fly appears at top left, and a fly is drawn near the verses. Students should notice how the verses and the web image frame the noble as a predator who feeds on the labour of the poor peasant.
text: Plus on a de moyens, plus on en veut avoir / Ce pauvre apporte tout, bled, fruit, argent, volaille / Ce gros Atilord assis, prest a tout receuoir / Ne luy veut pas donner la douceur d'vne cuillerée / A tous Seigneurs tous honneurs. / Maigre comme un leurier d'attache. / Il faut plier ou agréer. / a la mouche / que volle / il ne faut / point dans la toile
